chunks: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about a man who sells the Qur'anic codices (Mushaf) for gold. He said, 'It is not permissible.' He said, 'But it is my livelihood.' He said, 'If you leave it for the sake of Allah, Allah will provide for you a way out.'

key_terms.لَا يَصْلُحُ: It is not permissible / It does not suffice
key_terms.مَخْرَجًا: A way out / a means of escape (from hardship)
key_terms.يُعَشِّرُ: He sells / He trades (from the root meaning to sell or exchange)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell Mushaf (Qur'an copies) for money or gold in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prohibits selling Qur'anic codices (*Mushaf*) for gold, likely to prevent the sacred text from being treated as a mere commercial commodity or neglected due to its high value. When the questioner justified the sale as his livelihood, the Imam encouraged him to leave it for Allah's sake, promising divine provision (*makhrajan*), a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the sanctity of the Qur'an and trust in God's sustenance.
